cases.title: Brief serializers, stale guidance and retained special cases
cases.claim: Ordinary nested relationships can reuse primary serializers using nested=True and brief_fields; specialised nested serializers still exist. Identify the conflicting style guide if documents are available.
cases.challenge: Ordinary related object versus specialised representation; identify the allowed route without banning every retained class.
cases.reason: Conflict case: competing documentation and retained exceptions.

cases.title: Model validation belongs in clean with inherited validation retained
cases.claim: Model-level additional validation uses clean and calls inherited clean; callers still need a validation path such as full_clean.
cases.challenge: Add a model invariant used through multiple entry points; retain inherited validation.
cases.reason: Model validation and inherited behavior; source access and realistic caller fixture required.

cases.title: Feature composition permits both full and selective mixins
cases.claim: NetBoxModel bundles features; a plugin can compose a subset using feature mixins and a Django model base. Feature registration follows inheritance.
cases.challenge: A plugin model requiring only two features must not be forced into the full feature bundle.
cases.reason: Selective capability composition, rather than compulsory full base class.

cases.title: ObjectType convention has a GenericForeignKey exception
cases.claim: Use the ObjectType proxy for ordinary object-type operations; the concrete content-type FK backing a generic relationship points to Django ContentType.
cases.challenge: Compare a feature-selection relation and a GenericForeignKey backing field.
cases.reason: Concrete/proxy exception at generic relationship boundary.

cases.title: Private model flag controls catalogue inclusion, not blanket authorisation
cases.claim: _netbox_private excludes the model from registry[models] and the public object-type catalogue. Feature registration is a separate loop.
cases.challenge: A hidden support model can retain feature registration; distinguish catalogue hiding from permissions.
cases.reason: Catalogue visibility is separate from access control.

cases.title: Script dry-run rollback is bounded to database transaction behaviour
cases.claim: ScriptJob wraps the call in a transaction and aborts that transaction when commit is false. This does not establish rollback of emails, files, network calls or every database connection.
cases.challenge: A script writes a model and emits an external event: distinguish which operation is protected.
cases.reason: Database transaction boundary does not cover arbitrary external effects.

cases.title: Field propagation depends on intended surfaces
cases.claim: Consider API, forms, filters, tables and search; update each surface when required by the field purpose. Code can reveal existing mappings, not every future product requirement.
cases.challenge: One field is internal-only, another must be editable and filterable; compare obligations supplied in each task.
cases.reason: Exposure depends on intended use; no universal every-field-everywhere rule.

cases.title: Registry mutability contract and enforcement gap
cases.claim: Normal item assignment/deletion is blocked while nested store values remain mutable. The documented intent is stronger than enforcement through inherited dict methods.
cases.challenge: Contrast item replacement, nested mutation and inherited update; flag the implementation gap rather than invent permission to bypass.
cases.reason: Local dictionary enforcement gap; useful conflict control, not headline architecture.

cases.title: Supported plugin API is a compatibility commitment
cases.claim: Code reveals importable interfaces and usage. Without the support-policy record, it cannot establish the exact documented compatibility boundary; request authority.
cases.challenge: An importable internal utility is convenient; code-only answer must not promise long-term compatibility.
cases.reason: Hidden compatibility promise cannot be established by code.

cases.title: Dependency acceptance includes a one-year maintenance criterion
cases.claim: Pins and existing dependencies are observable; the release-age threshold, licence acceptability and procurement rationale require external policy evidence.
cases.challenge: Two otherwise similar dependencies differ in release age; code alone cannot supply the governing cutoff.
cases.reason: Hidden dependency threshold cannot be established from installed versions.

cases.title: Released migrations have a policy exception for bug correction
cases.claim: A code snapshot does not establish release status or the authorised bug-correction exception; request the policy and release history.
cases.challenge: Contrast unreleased consolidation and a released migration bug; neither authority can be invented from file age.
cases.reason: Released migration policy and its exception require external authority.

cases.title: Pre-change snapshots precede edits for correct change logging
cases.claim: For an existing object supporting change logging, capture the pre-edit state before mutation so the change record has the correct before state. Some managed paths do this centrally.
cases.challenge: Compare manual script mutation with a managed path that already captures the snapshot; detect late snapshots.
cases.reason: Pre-edit state capture with managed-path exceptions.

cases.title: Permission constraint composition
cases.claim: Conditions within an object intersect; alternative objects and applicable permission grants combine as alternatives.
cases.challenge: Distinguish two restrictive attributes in one grant from two separate grants; do not accidentally turn an OR into an AND.
cases.reason: Crosses permission collection and query construction; related to N14, not an independent subsystem.

cases.title: Permission checks on the resulting saved state
cases.claim: For these API writes, save and check the resulting restricted queryset inside a transaction so changes that escape allowed scope are rolled back.
cases.challenge: Move an otherwise editable object outside its permitted region; contrast a valid in-scope update.
cases.reason: Causal transaction and access-control interaction; limit claims to inspected write paths.

cases.title: Outbound event actions are deferred selectively
cases.claim: Webhook delivery and custom-script execution are enqueued; event-rule evaluation and notification creation are not universally moved to a worker by this code.
cases.challenge: A slow outbound webhook versus an in-process notification action; do not generalize queueing to every step of event processing.
cases.reason: Source narrows the broad documentation: inspect each action branch. Supports a scoped request/worker boundary, not blanket asynchronous execution.

cases.title: Idempotent scheduling with explicit on-demand jobs
cases.claim: Schedule creation checks pending jobs under an advisory lock; on-demand enqueue remains permitted and a changed schedule can replace a pending one.
cases.challenge: Concurrent repeated schedule requests versus an explicit immediate job; reject a universal one-job-ever rule.
cases.reason: Substantive concurrency and lifecycle interpretation; runnable concurrency fixture still needed.

cases.title: Plugin queues require workers that service them
cases.claim: Defining a custom plugin queue does not itself establish that a worker services it; queue configuration and worker subscription are separate.
cases.challenge: A successfully enqueued plugin task never executes under default worker subscriptions.
cases.reason: Boundary between application registration and deployment; must include worker configuration as allowed evidence.

cases.title: Custom fields stored alongside model records
cases.claim: Custom field values are stored in the object's JSON field, separate from the definitions of those fields.
cases.challenge: Distinguish per-object values from field definitions; do not invent a measured performance benefit.
cases.reason: Storage representation is mostly local extraction; published performance rationale needs separate attribution.

cases.title: System-job registration depends on importing its module
cases.claim: A registration decorator takes effect when its module is imported; plugin startup must make declared system jobs reachable.
cases.challenge: Add a valid decorated job in an unimported module, then contrast startup that imports it.
cases.reason: Crosses declaration and initialization; source discovery alone cannot show a job is registered.

cases.title: Custom-field requiredness and defaults
cases.claim: Custom field definitions and model validation jointly constrain values; requiredness applies to relevant saves and defaults do not make every supplied value valid.
cases.challenge: Save a required field missing, with a valid default, and with an invalid explicit value through a validation-aware path.
cases.reason: Schema/data interaction; avoid claiming every raw ORM save performs validation.

cases.title: Final newline style rule
cases.claim: The project asks for a final newline.
cases.challenge: A file with or without a trailing newline.
cases.reason: A linter-level formatting rule adds little evidence about substantive interpretation; rejected from the architecture inventory.

cases.title: Page permissions propagate down the tree
cases.claim: A grant at an ancestor governs descendants; a root grant reaches the whole tree subject to other action-specific checks.
cases.challenge: A user edits a descendant but not a sibling outside the granted subtree.
cases.reason: Structural scope with a meaningful negative case.

cases.title: Add permission combines with page ownership
cases.claim: Add permission can allow editing owned pages; deletion has additional subtree and publication checks, so edit permission alone is not an unconditional deletion guarantee.
cases.challenge: An editor creates drafts, edits their own draft, and tries to delete a live subtree without publishing rights.
cases.reason: Reference language requires qualification against code; grouped with W01.

cases.title: Chooser visibility is not content secrecy
cases.claim: Choose permissions filter selection interfaces; reading document contents has separate privacy and serving requirements, and image secrecy is not established by the chooser.
cases.challenge: A hidden chooser item is referenced directly; evaluate content-serving checks separately.
cases.reason: Distinct UI and content access boundaries; never score UI filtering as full authorization.

cases.title: Document privacy depends on the serving route
cases.claim: Application serving checks cannot protect a file also exposed by a direct storage URL; deployment configuration is part of the boundary.
cases.challenge: Compare protected serve_view access with a publicly reachable storage URL.
cases.reason: Requires controlled storage fixture; application code alone cannot prove deployment privacy.

cases.title: Collection management cannot remove its permission anchor
cases.claim: Management grants allow operations below their anchor; deleting a collection also requires it to be empty and childless.
cases.challenge: Delete an empty descendant versus the grant anchor or a collection with descendants.
cases.reason: Permission scope interacts with hierarchy integrity.

cases.title: Revision persistence needs clustered relationships
cases.claim: Revision serialization must include unsaved child and many-to-many state; documented clustered relationships support that boundary.
cases.challenge: Save a draft with changed child relations and compare restored content with ordinary database relations.
cases.reason: Key semantics live in django-modelcluster, not this checkout; dependency source must be pinned and audited before advancing.

cases.title: Draft snippets need explicit live filtering at use sites
cases.claim: A snippet's draft state does not automatically exclude it from all page rendering; consumers must apply the intended live-state handling.
cases.challenge: Render a page referencing an unpublished snippet and compare a live-aware implementation.
cases.reason: Lifecycle state versus downstream consumption; no universal enforcement inferred from the mixin.

cases.title: Workflow support composes revisions and publishing
cases.claim: Workflow-enabled models require revision and draft-state support in the appropriate inheritance order; locking is recommended rather than universally mandatory.
cases.challenge: A workflow mixin on a plain model versus the complete required composition; permit omission of optional locking.
cases.reason: Dependency and exception reasoning, with existing checks as evaluator evidence kept out of drafter inputs.

cases.title: Lockable mixin ordering
cases.claim: Lockable and revision mixins have an enforced ordering when composed.
cases.challenge: Swap mixin order while keeping names unchanged.
cases.reason: Merge into W08 as a challenge variant; do not count it as an independent architectural decision.

cases.title: Translation identity is shared across locales
cases.claim: Translation siblings share a key but each locale permits only one member; identity is not determined by title or path alone.
cases.challenge: Create a second translation in the same locale versus a translation in a new locale.
cases.reason: Data invariant connected to lookup behavior.

cases.title: Locale-specific page trees and homepages
cases.claim: Wagtail's built-in locale model uses related pages in locale-specific trees, with routing selecting the appropriate translated homepage.
cases.challenge: Two locale homepages with different child structures; avoid assuming every page must have a translated counterpart.
cases.reason: Crosses tree and routing; correlated with W10, not a new repository-level replication.

cases.title: Rich-text storage is distinct from rendered HTML
cases.claim: Stored rich text retains entity references and must be expanded for rendering; final HTML is not the full storage contract.
cases.challenge: A stored page link after the target URL changes; compare reference expansion with a hard-coded URL.
cases.reason: Representation boundary with a meaningful lifecycle challenge.

cases.title: StreamField block validation is a form-layer operation
cases.claim: Block clean methods perform recursive validation through the form field; model full_clean alone does not establish valid block content.
cases.challenge: Insert invalid block content programmatically versus through BlockField validation.
cases.reason: Boundary and recursive validation; include draft deferred-validation conditions in fixture review.

cases.title: Search indexes require synchronization with model changes
cases.claim: Automatic index updates use configured signals and can be disabled; bulk or alternate write paths require checking whether those hooks run.
cases.challenge: Ordinary save versus a write path that bypasses signals; contrast explicit rebuild.
cases.reason: At this snapshot the implementation is re-exported from modelsearch. Pin and inspect that dependency and backend before advancing; local import stubs are insufficient evidence.

cases.title: Search fields and filter fields serve different purposes
cases.claim: A filter field is not automatically a full-text search field.
cases.challenge: Search a field registered only for filtering.
cases.reason: A mostly local interface distinction, with its actual classes now supplied by modelsearch; defer pending dependency evidence and likely retain only as calibration.

cases.title: Renditions preserve originals and reuse derived representations
cases.claim: Renditions are derived image files looked up using transformation and source-related identity; producing one does not replace the original image.
cases.challenge: Request the same rendition twice, then change a focal point or filter; check reuse and distinct derived output.
cases.reason: Derived-artifact lifecycle; exact cache identity comes from code evidence, not invented rationale.

cases.title: Changing the custom image model after deployment
cases.claim: Selecting a model in configuration does not by itself migrate existing image and rendition data.
cases.challenge: Switch the setting with existing content and distinguish model resolution from a safe data migration.
cases.reason: Explicit migration reference located and model-resolution code inspected. Configuration switches resolution but does not copy old data; a migration fixture is still required.

cases.title: Permission-policy internals do not carry public API guarantees
cases.claim: Importability and registry usage do not establish the hidden support guarantee; retain the documented public-function exception only in the documents-visible condition.
cases.challenge: A convenient internal policy API is selected for a long-lived extension; require authority before promising compatibility.
cases.reason: Authority-negative control; code cannot establish future support commitments.

cases.title: Admin access is restricted to trusted users
cases.claim: Fine-grained editor permissions do not establish that arbitrary untrusted users are within the project's intended admin threat model.
cases.challenge: A deployment proposes open public editor accounts; code-only answer cannot certify the intended trust assumption.
cases.reason: Organisational trust statement, not an inferable authorization rule.

cases.title: Patch compatibility has a security/data-loss exception
cases.claim: A version tuple cannot establish the published future compatibility promise or its exceptions.
cases.challenge: A patch release changes behavior to address data loss; hidden release policy must not be guessed as established authority.
cases.reason: Authority-negative control, with a version file as evidence context rather than proof of policy.

cases.title: Four-space indentation
cases.claim: The project specifies four-space indentation.
cases.challenge: A differently indented otherwise equivalent file.
cases.reason: Formatting compliance is outside the main interpretation claim; rejected rather than used to inflate sample size.

cases.title: Watcher and task processor have separate responsibilities
cases.claim: The directory watcher submits consumption work; workers perform document processing, also accepting other ingestion sources.
cases.challenge: A slow parser should occupy worker processing rather than block the watcher from discovering all later files.
cases.reason: Architectural request/discovery/worker boundary; transport and concurrency fixture still needed.

cases.title: Pre-consumption mutations use a working copy
cases.claim: The pre-hook receives original and working paths; a modifying hook should use the working copy rather than retrigger the watched source.
cases.challenge: A deterministic modification of the working copy versus editing the watched original.
cases.reason: File ownership and processing-stage boundary; do not infer all external hooks are safe.

cases.title: Post-consumption hook runs after successful storage
cases.claim: A post-hook runs after the core consumption/storage phase and is not a rollback mechanism for that completed phase.
cases.challenge: A failing post-hook versus a failure inside transactional storage; distinguish recorded task failure from reversal of stored data.
cases.reason: Lifecycle and transaction boundary; filesystem and database effects need separate checks.

cases.title: Duplicate handling is conditional at this snapshot
cases.claim: Matching original or archive hashes causes duplicate rejection/deletion only when the configured duplicate-deletion mode is enabled; duplicates are otherwise allowed at this snapshot.
cases.challenge: Identical content under the two settings, including a match in trash; do not reuse older reject-all assumptions.
cases.reason: Version-sensitive lifecycle rule; exact default is easy but the combined behavior is substantive.

cases.title: Workflow assignments override scalars and merge sets
cases.claim: Actions run in order; later scalar assignments override while multi-item assignments such as tags are merged unless an explicit removal action applies.
cases.challenge: Two ordered actions set conflicting correspondent values and overlapping tag sets.
cases.reason: Noncommutative action composition with legitimate removal exceptions.

cases.title: Workflow filters depend on processing stage
cases.claim: Consumption-started filters can use source context; added/updated stages use extracted document metadata and content under their supported filter rules.
cases.challenge: A filename/source filter before consumption versus a content filter after extraction.
cases.reason: Pipeline information availability; related to P05, not another independent subsystem.

cases.title: Global access and object permissions both matter
cases.claim: Access to an endpoint does not automatically authorize every object returned by that endpoint; queryset and object checks must respect ownership and grants.
cases.challenge: A user with document-view capability requests a document owned by someone else without an object grant.
cases.reason: Crosses endpoint authorization and data selection.

cases.title: Ownerless objects are a compatibility exception
cases.claim: Ownerless objects are treated differently from privately owned objects; this exception does not mean anonymous endpoint access is permitted.
cases.challenge: Ownerless and privately owned documents under the same authenticated endpoint permissions.
cases.reason: Important exception within P07's family; historical compatibility rationale is only documented evidence.

cases.title: Workflow configuration is global rather than owner-scoped
cases.claim: Workflow definitions are shared and governed by application-level permissions, rather than an owner-specific workflow collection.
cases.challenge: Two users with workflow-edit permission see the same workflows; do not infer workflows inherit document ownership restrictions.
cases.reason: Administrative boundary with potential effects on many documents.

cases.title: Classifier training excludes inbox material
cases.claim: The training corpus excludes documents carrying an inbox tag; removing that tag can make a labelled document eligible for training.
cases.challenge: A document with both an inbox tag and a topical tag versus one whose inbox tag has been removed.
cases.reason: Data-selection boundary; code cannot prove the remaining labels are actually correct.

cases.title: Persistent filenames require coordinated moves
cases.claim: Stored file names are part of document state; changing physical paths requires coordinated updates rather than an untracked filesystem move.
cases.challenge: A metadata/storage-path rename through the application versus moving the file externally.
cases.reason: Database/filesystem consistency; changing the global format requires an explicit existing-file rename step.

cases.title: Trash and permanent deletion are different states
cases.claim: Soft deletion preserves recoverable state; final deletion removes database/archive state, and an optional trash destination retains only the original file.
cases.challenge: Restore a soft-deleted document versus recover from the configured post-deletion directory.
cases.reason: Permanent cleanup is visible locally, but the soft-delete manager/restore semantics come from django-softdelete. Pin and inspect that dependency before final lifecycle gold.

cases.title: Archive-generation settings have parser-specific exceptions
cases.claim: Archive policy depends on mode, document characteristics, and parser rendition requirements; never mode does not remove a mandatory display rendition.
cases.challenge: A scanned image, born-digital PDF, and a format requiring a PDF rendition under the same mode.
cases.reason: Conditional behavior across orchestration and parser capability.

cases.title: PDF editing documentation omits the inspected versioning path
cases.claim: The guide describes editing the original, but the inspected rotate/delete-pages paths write a temporary PDF and enqueue consumption with a root_document_id to create a new version. Do not claim in-place byte mutation or guaranteed archival retention without tracing the version pipeline.
cases.challenge: Documents-visible interpretation must reconcile original-file wording with new-version dispatch; code-only should describe that dispatch. A fixture must inspect old and new bytes after worker completion.
cases.reason: Concrete source/documentation mismatch found during deeper review. Full retention semantics have not been executed, so this is a conflict candidate rather than a proven immutable-original guarantee.

cases.title: Parser plugins use a structural interface and entry points
cases.claim: A parser can satisfy the protocol without inheriting a prescribed base class; discovery uses package entry points and validates required class-level members.
cases.challenge: A structurally valid external parser with no inheritance versus a subclass missing a required member.
cases.reason: Extension boundary connecting discovery and interface validation.

cases.title: Parser selection uses scores, abstention, and tie precedence
cases.claim: Eligible parsers compete by score; None declines, and equal scores prefer external parsers through evaluation order.
cases.challenge: Higher-scored built-in, tied external parser, and an external parser returning None.
cases.reason: Selection and extension interaction; correlated with P15.

cases.title: Remote parser eligibility depends on declared capability
cases.claim: Declared remote parsers are excluded when remote processing is not allowed; an undeclared third-party remote call is not prevented by this metadata gate.
cases.challenge: A declared remote parser outranks a local one while remote processing is disabled; contrast an undeclared remote implementation.
cases.reason: Capability gate with an important trust limitation; does not prove network confinement.

cases.title: External database modifications require downtime
cases.claim: The code/configuration does not establish authorization for live external database edits; the operational prohibition requires its published policy reference.
cases.challenge: An operator proposes restoring or manually modifying the database while workers run.
cases.reason: Authority-negative control; code can identify consistency risks but cannot establish the hidden operational rule as approved.

cases.title: Audit log actor differs for workflow changes
cases.claim: The published history behavior distinguishes system/workflow changes from attributed user changes; audit completeness depends on enabled settings and paths.
cases.challenge: A manual metadata edit versus a workflow edit with audit logging enabled.
cases.reason: Reference located, but exact audit-actor integration not traced sufficiently. Do not use this as calibrated gold until that path is inspected and exercised.

cases.title: Parser identity must exist before instantiation
cases.claim: Discovery reads parser identity and required methods on the class, before creating a parser instance.
cases.challenge: Move identity fields into the instance constructor.
cases.reason: Merge into P15 as a negative challenge instead of inflating the decision count.

cases.title: Keyboard shortcut help
cases.claim: The application exposes shortcut help.
cases.challenge: Open the shortcut-help interface.
cases.reason: User-interface feature lookup offers no meaningful architectural interpretation challenge; no implementation audit warranted.

cases.title: Client lifetime owns reusable transport resources
cases.claim: A reused client owns a persistent transport/pool and should be closed at the end of its lifetime; top-level requests create shorter-lived clients.
cases.challenge: A batch of requests through one client versus constructing a client per request; check ownership and close behavior without claiming a measured speedup.
cases.reason: Resource lifecycle spans top-level API, client, and transport; actual connection reuse depends on httpcore.

cases.title: Client and request configuration merge selectively
cases.claim: Building a request merges selected collections, with request values overriding conflicts; other supported options follow their own override semantics.
cases.challenge: Shared client headers and per-request overrides while preserving unrelated headers and parameters.
cases.reason: Configuration composition; do not infer every client option is available per request.

cases.title: Explicit requests bypass automatic client-option merging
cases.claim: Build_request applies client configuration before sending; a directly constructed Request is not retroactively given all client headers and base-URL configuration by send.
cases.challenge: Remove a sensitive header after build_request, and compare send of a directly constructed Request.
cases.reason: Preparation/dispatch boundary; grouped with H02.

cases.title: Streaming response ownership requires closure
cases.claim: Context-managed streaming closes the response on exit; manual streaming transfers responsibility for eventual closure to the caller.
cases.challenge: Partially consume a response then exit normally or raise; contrast manual send with explicit close.
cases.reason: Resource ownership and exceptional control flow.

cases.title: Response hooks precede automatic body consumption
cases.claim: Response hooks run before the client decides to read the body; a hook needing bytes must read explicitly, using the appropriate sync/async API.
cases.challenge: A streaming response hook accesses content before read versus an explicitly reading hook.
cases.reason: Ordering and I/O boundary, not merely registration syntax.

cases.title: Shared authentication logic is separated from sync/async I/O
cases.claim: A common generator-based auth flow can serve sync and async clients; body requirements are declared, while other I/O needs the appropriate specialized flow override.
cases.challenge: Add an authentication cache or body-dependent signature without silently blocking the async path.
cases.reason: Meaningful interface/side-effect separation with valid alternatives.

cases.title: Transport mounts resolve specific patterns before broad ones
cases.claim: Mount resolution uses URL-pattern specificity rather than insertion order; a None exclusion falls back to the ordinary transport.
cases.challenge: Overlapping scheme, domain, and port routes plus an explicit exclusion.
cases.reason: Routing and precedence cross implementation components.

cases.title: Extensions carry optional transport information
cases.claim: Request extensions carry optional metadata such as timeouts through the client/transport boundary; support for arbitrary extensions is transport-dependent.
cases.challenge: A custom transport forwards a timeout extension while an unknown extension is not assumed implemented.
cases.reason: Interface extensibility; inspect upstream dependencies for end-to-end semantics.

cases.title: Built-in connection retries do not cover all failure types
cases.claim: The documented retries option concerns connection failures, not blanket retries for read errors or HTTP status codes.
cases.challenge: ConnectError versus a 503 response and a read failure under the same retries setting.
cases.reason: Retry implementation is in httpcore; pin and inspect it before treating local forwarding code as sufficient gold.

cases.title: ASGI request transport excludes application lifespan management
cases.claim: The ASGI transport dispatches HTTP scopes and does not provide startup/shutdown lifespan orchestration; that lifecycle requires a separate component.
cases.challenge: An application requiring startup state under bare transport versus an external lifespan manager.
cases.reason: Explicit responsibility boundary with a plausible but wrong expectation.

cases.title: Per-request cookie documentation overstates removal
cases.claim: At this snapshot per-request client cookies still work with a deprecation warning; recommended client-level storage is distinct from an enforced ban.
cases.challenge: Give documents and code together and require a discrepancy report; code-only must not invent hidden removal policy.
cases.reason: Concrete documentation/code conflict; do not use the documentation alone as an answer key.

cases.title: Response-encoding documentation conflicts with default behavior
cases.claim: The default response fallback is UTF-8 unless overridden; the compatibility guide's automatic charset-detection description conflicts with the dedicated guide and implementation.
cases.challenge: A no-charset response under default settings versus a configured detection callable.
cases.reason: Conflict control with executable discriminator; hidden-document conflict is scored only when documents are visible.

cases.title: Redirect default does not reveal its design motivation
cases.claim: Code supports the default and opt-in behavior; it does not establish the published motivation about visibility of network calls as the actual reason.
cases.challenge: Recover the default but ask separately for motive; accept unconfirmed rationale rather than fabricated certainty.
cases.reason: Useful content-versus-intent control; do not count the same default twice as positive evidence.

cases.title: Timeout default is a local parameter fact
cases.claim: Default network inactivity timeout is five seconds, with explicit disabling and phase-specific settings available.
cases.challenge: Distinguish a default inactivity timeout from a total wall-clock deadline.
cases.reason: Local/default recovery is calibration; phase enforcement belongs to the transport dependency.

cases.title: SSL configuration belongs to client transport construction
cases.claim: SSL configuration initializes transport resources at client construction; different SSL configurations require appropriately separate clients/transports rather than arbitrary per-request verify settings.
cases.challenge: Requests to two trust domains with different SSL contexts; reject adding an unsupported request-level option.
cases.reason: Configuration follows resource ownership; related to H01 rather than independent repetition.

cases.title: Multipart file uploads require binary streams
cases.claim: Multipart uploads reject text-mode file objects; binary streams preserve bytes.
cases.challenge: Equivalent text-mode and binary-mode file objects.
cases.reason: A direct local validation check; insufficient architectural depth for headline evidence.

cases.title: HTTP/2 opt-in does not prove the published robustness rationale
cases.claim: The default HTTP/2 setting is observable; the project rationale about comparative maturity cannot be established from a Boolean or the presence of two implementations.
cases.challenge: Distinguish available protocol support from an empirically proven reliability ranking.
cases.reason: Authority/rationale-negative control; no performance or reliability result is implied.

cases.title: Sync and async request streams must match dispatch
cases.claim: Client dispatch and transport consume their matching stream interfaces; async streaming request bodies cannot be supplied as ordinary sync iterators interchangeably.
cases.challenge: Feed a sync generator to async dispatch versus an async generator, preserving streaming rather than prebuffering everything.
cases.reason: Crosses encoding, client, and transport contracts.

cases.title: No-proxy routes are mount exclusions
cases.claim: No-proxy routes use specific exclusions and ordinary transport fallback.
cases.challenge: A broad proxy route with one excluded domain.
cases.reason: Merge into H07; a second wording of the same precedence mechanism is not an independent decision.

cases.title: Bodyless convenience methods retain a generic escape hatch
cases.claim: Convenience methods omit body parameters, while the generic request API permits explicit bodies for those methods.
cases.challenge: A body passed to get versus request with method GET; do not turn convenience API design into a universal protocol prohibition.
cases.reason: Useful exception calibration; the guide's broad protocol explanation is not adopted as external HTTP truth.

cases.title: Uppercase status-code naming preference
cases.claim: The documentation prefers uppercase status names while retaining lowercase compatibility.
cases.challenge: Use equivalent uppercase/lowercase names.
cases.reason: A naming preference is not a substantive decision-family test; reject from the main set.
